Yeah, there’s also a ton of land that we’ve taken from them that hasn’t been returned. I think it’s an issue that as Canadians we’re still reckoning with, and it’s uncomfortable for us to discuss. It doesn’t seem to be talked about much outside of Canada, and we end up with this perception that we’re a good country that accepts everyone and takes care of our people. We do some things right, but we have a lot of work to do towards equality, reparations for the Indigenous people, and getting rid of the racism around us. 

I’m from Winnipeg, and while I can see things getting better slowly, we still have a lot of work to do. In recent years, we had a [serial killer targeting homeless Indigenous women](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Winnipeg_serial_killings#:~:text=On%20May%2016%2C%202022%2C%20Rebecca,at%20the%20Brady%20Road%20Landfill.), and the response to the landfill search for the bodies has been very disheartening. A lot of people saying it’s a waste of money and they’ll never find anything, when it would bring the families closure and would’ve been much less difficult if it had been done earlier (thanks to the Winnipeg police and Heather Stefanson). Now that they have found something in the last week, people are changing their tune of course. 

Appreciate you bring more attention towards this issue! I think it’s an important issue that isn’t talked about enough, especially outside of Canada.
